description.narrative: Through this project, Oxfam and RECA will develop a practical multi-hazard decision-making model for anticipatory action that includes the risk of economic shocks as one of the main drivers of humanitarian need to enable vulnerable groups to mitigate the impact of shocks on their lives and livelihoods. Embedding economic shocks in a multi-hazard model requires investment since the methodologyisn't readily available to understand and forecast economic shocks, and will need to be developed through this project. However, this can build on available economic and vulnerability indicators that are already used in humanitarian programming, especially in protracted crisis contexts, and that are used in social protection programming. The multi-hazard model will build on existing work in anticipatory action and social protection, and it will combine economic vulnerability with other (contextual) drivers of humanitarianneed. It may therefore include indicators for both climate-induced and human-made hazards.The proposed model for multi-hazard anticipatory action will consider that economic shocks and economic vulnerability can manifest in different ways, but also how economic vulnerability can be a driver of humanitarian need. In this context, (household) economic vulnerability refers to the coping capacityof a household to withstand shocks, including unexpected or increased expenses or income fluctuations. This project will have two main results, with the first result focusing on the development of the multi-hazard anticipatory action model, and the second result focuses on documentation of the process of developing the model for sector-wide influencing. While the project will focus on the Nigerien context, the process of the development of the multi-hazard AA model will be used to demonstrate the relevance of economic shocks in anticipatory action and influence stakeholders in the sector to take a similar approach. The project focuses on the process of developing a multi-hazard anticipatory action model and it does not include the implementation of activities based on activation of the model.

participating-org.narrative: The Réseau National des Chambres d'Agriculture du Niger represents the interests of the entire agricultural profession. As such, its main missions are to : a) Coordinate the activities of the regional Chambers of Agriculture at national level;b) Represent the regional Chambers of Agriculture in dealings with public authorities and all national and international public and private institutions;c) Present proposals on ways to develop agro-sylvo-pastoral activities;d) To encourage the creation of professional associations, groupings and any other organizations related to the activities listed above, with a view to their promotion;e) To act as a technicalassistant to its members, providing them with legal, administrative and accounting advice, and to maintain an up-to-date database of agro-sylvo-pastoral businesses, associations, groups and production organizations;f) Collect, produce and disseminate economic andprofessional information on the above activities;To this end, it may set up services or establishments responsible for management assistance and training;Receive notification from the competent judicial and administrative authorities of any registration of changes in the trade register of agro-sylvo-pastoral companies and any act of recognition offarmers' organizations, associations and groups;h) To ensure, subject to compliance with the laws and regulations in force, the administration of services and, where necessary, the execution of work required by the interests for which it is responsible;i)Make suggestions to the Administration concerning training, organization and professional orientation in the rural sector;j) Propose any modifications to the Chamber Network to the Government for approval.
